tasks.title: Separate CI N/A from retained changed-line evidence

Explicit true retained-evidence mode still requires an explicit valid base, direct or merge-base semantics, a nonzero executable denominator, and at least 90 percent coverage; it never degrades to N/A.

When auto mode has a nonzero executable denominator it still enforces the 90 percent floor, including mixed executable and non-executable changes without counting deleted or comment-only lines as executable evidence.

Policy tests cover documentation-only, comment-only, deletion-only, rename, untracked, mixed executable/non-executable, passing and failing executable percentages, and explicit retained-evidence behavior.

tasks.title: Bound retained Runs and creation keys with ownership-safe GC
tasks.objective: Give a long-lived daemon an explicit global retained-state budget and exited-Run collection policy whose memory, CPU, thread, descriptor, replay, and key semantics remain measurable under sustained churn.
tasks.outcome: Exited Run records and creation keys no longer grow without bound; protected live or pinned owners are never collected, and retained replay is discarded only with one eligible terminal Run under a documented fail-closed contract.
acceptance: One reviewed retention contract fixes one exact global Run-record ceiling, deterministic candidate order and tie-breaks, trigger points, temporary-owner treatment, running Runs, lookup-to-pin ownership, exited replay, creation flights and keys, persistent rows, collection eligibility, and observable post-collection errors before implementation; the total replay bound is derived from that ceiling and the existing per-Run retention contract rather than a second hot-path byte quota.

Start, Fork, and tmux import collect eligible terminal Runs before exceeding the global Run-record ceiling; when running, attached, pinned, or other protected owners exhaust capacity, admission returns a typed capacity error before native physical launch or Backend publication instead of crossing the bound.

Eligibility requires quiescent native reader, waiter and control ownership, tmux control, attachment lookup-to-pin, fresh Fork lookup, same-key retry lookup, input drain, terminal publication, reader completion, and persistence transition; lookup-to-pin admission is atomic against collection, and deterministic barriers cover each lookup or completion racing collection.

An unpublished-child cleanup or exact-key fence retained by T-026 is a protected owner: collection cannot release its key, hide it from bounded accounting, or make it eligible for a second physical launch.

One exact candidate fence prevents new pins, then one Registry transition removes an eligible retained Run and all of its operation-key mappings together without a stale lookup or duplicate physical-process window.

Persistent collection first fences the exact candidate, deletes its row, owned replay, key and accounting in one SQLite transaction, restores eligibility on pre-COMMIT failure, and after COMMIT performs an exact non-failing Registry removal; injected failures and restart around COMMIT recover only fully present or fully absent state.

Collection preserves immutable descendant lineage even when its parent RunId becomes a dangling historical reference; a retained child's same-key Fork retry still resolves before parent lookup, while a fresh-key Fork against a collected parent returns run_not_found.

After collection, List omits the Run, Status and Attach report run_not_found, and a fresh-key Fork naming it reports run_not_found; the old operation key may create a new physical Run only after its prior Run is absent from every retained owner, and clients receive no silent replay or continuity claim.

Deterministic memory-only and persistent churn workloads cross the production budget for at least three collection windows and prove pre-registered non-growth for core-normalized CPU, collection work and latency, peak and steady RSS, retained bytes, Run/key count, threads, descriptors, child, attachment, reader, waiter, and input-drain ownership; restart recovers the same retained set and key mappings.

Historical observe receipts, hashes, runtime identities, and every numeric frozen ceiling remain unchanged; current qualification declares the new GC/admission contract separately, and no shortened soak, rebaseline, or post-result margin change replaces canonical nightly evidence.

The policy adds no Agent/session metadata, scheduler, distributed lease, public Backend hierarchy, arbitrary TTL compatibility layer, or budget relaxation; SSH, Signal/process-tree, and Runtime identity negotiation remain separate capabilities.

verification.proves: Registry, persistence, replay, key reuse, and public collection regressions pass.

A clean canonical nightly qualification records at least three collection windows, CPU and memory plateaus, the frozen 1/32/128 resource matrix, source identity, receipt hashes, and unchanged budget hashes.
The exact clean commit, canonical nightly receipt and hash, raw plateau series, and unchanged frozen-budget hash are bound to T-027 completion.
